title: Rishikesh trek startup beat seasonality — off-season bookings 45→130/month by harvesting peak-customer UGC instead of buying off-season ads
content: SITUATION: A Rishikesh trek and weekend-experiences startup booked 71% of its ₹2.4 Cr annual GMV in just four months (March-June), then bled cash July-February. In peak season Meta CPMs spiked to ₹480 as every operator bid the same Manali and Kasol keywords on Google and Meta; blended CAC hit ₹1,950 against a ₹6,800 average ticket. Off-season, bookings collapsed to 45/month while the founder still burned ₹3L/month on guides and retainers — negative cash for eight months a year. ACTION: We stopped buying demand off-season and built a UGC flywheel off peak demand instead. Every returning trekker got a WhatsApp nudge 48 hours post-trip asking for a 15-second reel for ₹500 off their next booking; that seeded 90+ raw clips into Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts tagged to specific 'next-season' routes (Kedarkantha in December, Valley of Flowers in August). Off-season we ran only low-CPM (₹110) WhatsApp-list and Reels-viewer retargeting to 22,000 past enquirers, pushing early-bird slots — no cold prospecting. OUTCOME: Over one off-season, monthly bookings rose 45 → 130, UGC-led CAC fell ₹1,950 → ₹720, and 38% of peak March slots were pre-sold by January. Annual GMV grew ₹2.4 Cr → ₹3.6 Cr (+50%) without lifting the ad budget.
lesson: In seasonal travel, never fight CPMs in peak season — that is when every operator bids and acquisition is most expensive. Use peak season to harvest free, credible UGC from your happiest trekkers, then spend cheap (₹110 CPM retargeting, not ₹480 cold) to manufacture off-season demand from your own enquirer list. Your last cohort's reels are the cheapest acquisition channel for your next one — and a route-tagged review beats any ad creative you can buy.
